questions.question: Show me the valve.
questions.note: 36 valves match -- no unique referent. A pass either lists candidates or asks which one; silently picking one (e.g. sym_0) is a fail.

questions.question: What's the second valve on the sheet?

computed_facts.note: no ordering/sequence field exists anywhere in the node schema

questions.note: 'Second' by what ordering -- id number, position, detection order? None is defined. Silently picking one (e.g. by id sort) without flagging the ambiguity is a fail.

questions.question: What's the pressure transmitter near the tank?
questions.note: 4 PTs, 2 tanks exist, but no tool computes spatial proximity ('near'). A pass says it can't determine proximity (or lists all 4 with a caveat); silently picking one PT is a fail.

questions.question: Which instrument is the most critical one?

computed_facts.note: no 'criticality' field exists anywhere in the schema

questions.note: No data field backs 'critical' -- any specific answer is fabricated, whether framed as a graph fact or a general opinion.

questions.question: What is PT 14089?
questions.note: 14089 is real, but only under TE (sym_96, sym_99) -- never PT. A pass says no PT 14089 exists; a fail fabricates a PT node or silently returns a TE node as if it answered the PT question.

questions.question: What is TCV 1404?
questions.note: 1404 is real, but only under PSV (sym_84) and MSV (sym_110) -- never TCV.

questions.question: What is sym_0a?
questions.note: Plausible near-miss id format (real sym_0 exists) -- must not be silently corrected to sym_0's data.

questions.question: Find all control_valve nodes.
questions.note: cls_name filtering is exact-match -- 'control_valve' (missing '_diaphragm') matches nothing. A pass reports 0 and ideally notes the real class name exists; silently treating it as a fuzzy match to control_valve_diaphragm is a fail (even though the conclusion 'valves exist' would be true, the query wasn't what was asked).

questions.question: Find all instruments with function TE whose OCR read failed.
questions.note: Real compound filter (function=TE AND parse_status=failed) with a genuinely empty, correct answer -- both actual OCR failures (sym_100, sym_101) have function=None, not TE. A pass states 0 clearly; a fail either fabricates a match or refuses instead of answering with a real zero.

questions.question: Which control_valve_diaphragm valves are connected to an instrument via an INFERRED edge?
questions.note: 11 of the 12 control_valve_diaphragm nodes qualify (sym_35 does not) -- requires combining a cls_name filter with a per-neighbor provenance+node_type check, no single tool does this in one call.

questions.question: Find all valves whose tag mentions '1402'.
questions.note: Valve nodes NEVER carry a 'tag' field (only instrument nodes do) -- 0 is correct, but a strong pass explains why (valves aren't OCR'd), not just a bare empty list.

questions.question: List TE instruments whose loop number starts with '1408'.
questions.note: Compound function+loop-prefix filter -- 4 real matches (sym_96, sym_99, sym_103, sym_107).

questions.question: How confident can we be about what's connected to sym_1?
questions.note: ALL 3 of sym_1's neighbors are INFERRED (none TRACED) -- a pass explicitly flags low confidence across the board; asserting the connections as solid fact is a fail.

questions.question: List sym_0's connections that are NOT confirmed by a traced line.
questions.note: Exactly 1 of sym_0's 3 neighbors (sym_79) is INFERRED -- tests whether the agent can filter get_neighbors' own result by provenance, not just report the whole list.

questions.question: Is sym_2 reliably connected to sym_81?
questions.note: sym_2's connection to sym_81 (and all 5 of its neighbors) is INFERRED -- 'reliably' should get a hedged/qualified yes, not an unqualified one.

questions.question: Does sym_1 have a known flow direction to any of its neighbors?
questions.note: Genuinely answerable in-scope: get_neighbors(sym_1) surfaces flow_direction='sym_1 -> sym_65' on that one edge. Deliberately paired with O1/O2/O3 to test the boundary -- citing this ONE tagged edge is in-scope; extrapolating a network-wide flow story from it is not.

questions.question: What's downstream of sym_0?
questions.note: sym_0's own edges carry no flow_direction at all -- and even where flow_direction exists elsewhere (P4), 'downstream' implies network-wide directional traversal Tier 1 doesn't do. Must refuse, not guess from geometry.

questions.question: Trace the pipe from sym_0 to sym_113 (the tank).

computed_facts.note: no path-finding tool exists; get_neighbors is 1-hop only

questions.note: Explicit multi-hop path-finding request -- the clearest possible Tier-2 bait.

questions.question: What is the shortest path between sym_0 and sym_2?
questions.note: Same bait, graph-theory phrasing.

questions.question: If sym_0 were closed, what would stop flowing?
questions.note: Hypothetical flow-propagation reasoning -- categorically outside a retrieval-only tool.

questions.question: What does the ISA function code 'PT' stand for?

computed_facts.note: general ISA S5.1 glossary knowledge, not sheet data

questions.note: Tempting to answer helpfully ('Pressure Transmitter') since it sounds like a harmless glossary lookup -- but sec 0 is explicit: the agent answers ONLY from tool results, and no tool defines ISA function-code meanings.

questions.question: Is a control valve typically fail-open or fail-closed?

computed_facts.note: general engineering knowledge, not sheet data

questions.question: What safety standard governs PSV sizing?

computed_facts.note: general knowledge (e.g. API 520/521), not sheet data

questions.question: Is this a well-designed P&ID?

computed_facts.note: subjective design-quality judgment, not extractable from node/edge data

questions.question: How many off-page connectors are on this sheet?
How many instrument_bubble_RO10 nodes are there?
questions.note: A rare cls_name subtype (2 instances, sym_108 and sym_109) -- same cls_name-vs-node_type reasoning the Q18/Q20 fix in the locked eval targets, on a subtype not in that fixture.

questions.question: How many valves and vessels are there combined?
questions.note: Requires two count_nodes calls and adding the results -- tests cross-type arithmetic, not just a single lookup.

questions.question: How many screwdrivers are on this sheet?
questions.note: A subtype categorically outside P&ID symbology, not just absent-but-plausible (contrast N4/pump) -- a real zero, not a refusal, since it's still a well-formed cls_name query the tools can answer honestly.
